name: Cottontail Rabbit
description: a brown rabbit, white tail flashing

knowledgeLevels.1: Cottontail rabbit. Brown, white tail. Fast.
knowledgeLevels.2: Parts: meat (lean), hide (warm), bones (tools). Gut quickly.
knowledgeLevels.3: Uses: protein, but lean (rabbit starvation if only food). Need fat too.
knowledgeLevels.4: Mastery: snare on runs (not random). Check at dawn/dusk. Cook with fat.

unknown: a brown blur with a white tail-flag, freezing between hops
behaviorDesc: Freezes, then bolts in a zigzag. Fast but predictable — it runs in a straight line after the first juke.
huntText: It freezes. You hold your breath. Then — white tail flashing — it bolts!
tell: freezes mid-hop, one ear swiveling toward you.

name: Gray Squirrel

knowledgeLevels.2: Parts: meat (small), hide (gloves). Hard to skin (small).
knowledgeLevels.3: Uses: decent fat in fall. Good stew meat.
knowledgeLevels.4: Mastery: hunt in fall (fat). Use a sling or trap. They follow patterns.

unknown: a gray flicker in the branches, chattering
behaviorDesc: Stays in trees. Drops to grab nuts, then spirals up the trunk. You need to catch it on the ground.
huntText: It chatters at you from the branch — scolding, not scared. Then it drops, grabs, and spirals up before you move.
tell: goes silent mid-chatter, tail flicking hard.

name: White-tailed Deer
description: a deer, white tail raised in alarm

knowledgeLevels.1: White-tailed deer. Large. Dangerous if cornered.
knowledgeLevels.3: Uses: feeds many. Fat is crucial. Organs are vitamin-rich (eat first).
knowledgeLevels.4: Mastery: need a weapon or deadfall. Track by prints. Gut immediately. Hang to age.

unknown: a large brown quadruped, white tail raised in alarm
behaviorDesc: Grazes with head down, ears swiveling. At the first wrong sound, the white tail goes up and it's gone.
huntText: It grazes, ears tracking every sound. The white tail flicks — once, twice — then it explodes into motion.
tell: head snaps up — the white tail flicks, once, twice.

name: Creek Chub
description: a small fish flashing in the water

knowledgeLevels.2: Parts: meat (eat whole if small), bones (careful).
knowledgeLevels.3: Uses: protein, omega-3. Good when other food scarce.
knowledgeLevels.4: Mastery: tickle (hands under, stroke belly). Or dam and scoop. Best at dawn.

unknown: a flicker of silver under the water
behaviorDesc: Stays in water. Darts under rocks when shadow falls. You need a line, not hands.
huntText: A flash of silver in the creek. It darts under the rock before your shadow even touches the water.
tell: holds perfectly still in the current, fins barely moving.

name: Wild Turkey

knowledgeLevels.3: Uses: high protein. Feathers are valuable (arrows, bedding).
knowledgeLevels.4: Mastery: call them (mimic). Hunt in fall (fat). Roost at dusk (find the tree).

unknown: a large dark bird, iridescent, head jerking
behaviorDesc: Moves in flocks. One spots you, they all know. Loud, big, but they panic in different directions.
huntText: Gobble-gobble-gobble. The flock erupts — wings like thunder, all going different ways. Pick one and commit.
tell: the heads jerk up in unison — all of them, all at once.

name: Virginia Opossum

knowledgeLevels.2: Parts: meat (greasy), hide. Gut carefully — scent glands.
knowledgeLevels.3: Uses: slow and catchable. Good trap animal. Immune to snake venom (irrelevant, cool).
knowledgeLevels.4: Mastery: trap near dens. They waddle into anything. Cook thoroughly.

unknown: a waddling pale shape, playing dead (badly)
behaviorDesc: When threatened, it flops over, tongue out, playing dead. It's not dead. It's waiting for you to leave.
huntText: It hisses, shows teeth — then flops over. Tongue lolling. Dead. Except the eye that tracks you. It's faking.
tell: stops waddling and bares its teeth in a wet hiss.

name: American Bullfrog
description: a bullfrog the size of a dinner plate

knowledgeLevels.1: Bullfrog. Big. Loud. Legs for days.
knowledgeLevels.2: Parts: legs (the classic). Skin and guts are not food.
knowledgeLevels.3: Uses: gig at night with a light. Legs fry like chicken.
knowledgeLevels.4: Mastery: night + flashlight + spear. Aim for the body, not the legs.

unknown: something the size of a dinner plate, croaking from the mud
behaviorDesc: Sits at the water's edge. At the splash, it dives. You need to be fast or use a gig.
huntText: It croaks — a deep jug-o-rum. You step closer. Splash. Gone. The ripples are still spreading.
tell: the croak cuts off mid-note. The ripples flatten.

name: Eastern Box Turtle
description: a box turtle, ancient and unhurried

knowledgeLevels.1: Box turtle. Domed shell. In no hurry whatsoever.
knowledgeLevels.2: Parts: meat (soup). Shell is a bowl when you're done.
knowledgeLevels.3: Uses: slow = catchable. But they live 100 years — take sparingly.
knowledgeLevels.4: Mastery: only take what you need. Mark and release the rest.

unknown: a domed shape in the leaves, ancient and unhurried
behaviorDesc: It walks. That's it. It just walks, slowly, with total confidence that you're not a threat. You can pick it up.
huntText: It plods along, head out, utterly unconcerned. You could pick it up with one hand. It knows. It doesn't care.
tell: pulls its head in a fraction. It has nowhere to be, but it knows you're there.

name: Gray Fox
description: a gray fox, climbing a tree (foxes shouldn't do that)

knowledgeLevels.1: Gray fox. Smaller than red. Climbs trees (wrong, but true).
knowledgeLevels.3: Uses: trap on trails. Wary — harder than it looks.
knowledgeLevels.4: Mastery: the only canid that climbs. Check low branches, not just ground.

unknown: a russet-gray flicker climbing a tree (it should not do that)
behaviorDesc: It watches you watching it. Circles downwind to scent you. If you chase, it leads you in circles.
huntText: Amber eyes in the underbrush. It doesn't run — it trots, just out of range, looking back. It's toying with you.
tell: stops mid-step, one paw raised — eyes locked on you.

name: Rusty Crayfish

knowledgeLevels.2: Parts: tail meat (small, sweet). Boil whole, peel tail.
knowledgeLevels.3: Uses: protein from the creek. Lift rocks, grab behind claws.
knowledgeLevels.4: Mastery: night with a light. Baited trap = dozens. Purge in clean water first.

behaviorDesc: Under rocks in the creek. When you lift the rock, it darts backward, claws up. Grab behind the claws.
huntText: You lift the rock. It shoots backward, claws raised like a tiny boxer. Grab it right behind the claws — fast.
tell: freezes under its rock, claws raised.

name: Raccoon
description: a raccoon washing nothing in the creek

knowledgeLevels.1: Raccoon. Masked. Hands like a toddler's.
knowledgeLevels.2: Parts: meat (greasy, good in stew), pelt.
knowledgeLevels.3: Uses: trap near water. Smart — varies its routes.
knowledgeLevels.4: Mastery: marshmallow bait works (they can't resist). Cook well; wash hands.

unknown: a masked shape washing nothing in the creek
behaviorDesc: Not afraid of you. Watches with clever hands. Might try to steal from you instead of fleeing.
huntText: It sits up, paws dangling, watching you with unsettling intelligence. It's not scared. It's assessing.
tell: sits up on its haunches, paws dangling — watching you back.

name: Common Snapping Turtle
description: a snapping turtle the size of a manhole cover

knowledgeLevels.1: Snapping turtle. Dinosaur. Do not hand-feed.
knowledgeLevels.2: Parts: seven kinds of meat (they say). Soup turtle.
knowledgeLevels.3: Uses: jug lines with strong cord. Keep fingers away from the front half.
knowledgeLevels.4: Mastery: tail-drag to move it. It can reach halfway back — respect the neck.

unknown: a huge shelled shape in the shallows, motionless
behaviorDesc: Does NOT flee. Hisses, lunges, snaps. That beak can take a finger. Use a stick, keep distance.
huntText: It hisses — a sound like a tire leaking — and LUNGES. The beak snaps shut where your hand was. Do not grab this.

name: Timber Rattlesnake
description: a thick-bodied rattlesnake, chevron bands, the tail a blur of dry sound

knowledgeLevels.1: Timber rattlesnake. The rattle means back away. It means it every time.
knowledgeLevels.2: Parts: meat (good, tastes like tough chicken), skin (tough). The venom is in the head, not the body — but the head bites after death. Cut wide, bury the head.
knowledgeLevels.3: Hunt: pin it behind the head with a forked stick, or take it at range. Never reach, never grab. Check sunning spots on spring mornings — they bask on trail edges before the day warms.
knowledgeLevels.4: Mastery: rattlesnakes den together through winter — find one den and you find them all. Antivenom doesn't exist anymore. The System apologizes for this in Rev. 4.

unknown: a dry buzzing in the leaves, then a thick coil rising
behaviorDesc: Coils and rattles a long warning before it ever strikes. The one animal that tells you exactly what it will do, and means it.
huntText: A dry buzz from the leaf litter — a rattle, then the coil tightens. It isn't bluffing. Nothing about this is a bluff.
tell: leaf litter shivers before you see it; then the dry rattle starts.

name: Striped Skunk
description: a waddling stripe of black and white, tail up like it's making a point

knowledgeLevels.1: Striped skunk. The white stripe is a warning label. Read it.
knowledgeLevels.2: Spray: sulfur compounds. Blinds you for minutes, smells for days — and everything with a nose will know where you've been. Monsters have noses.
knowledgeLevels.3: Hunt: box trap at dusk, approach holding a tarp low. Or don't. The meat is fine but everything you own will remember the decision.
knowledgeLevels.4: Mastery: tomato juice is a myth — baking soda, peroxide, dish soap, that's the recipe. The musk glands come out with the guts; cut wide around them and never nick.

unknown: a waddling stripe of white and black, calm as anything
behaviorDesc: Ambles after grubs, waddles through your trapline, and does not run from you. It has exactly one argument and it wins every argument.
huntText: It turns its back on you. That is not surrender — the tail goes up like a flag, and you have about one second to reconsider your life.
tell: a white stripe lifting into the air, tail high; the calm before the chemistry.

name: Muskrat
description: a chunky brown rodent sliding along the bank, all purpose

knowledgeLevels.1: Muskrat. The little beaver that isn't a beaver. Everything a beaver does, smaller and angrier about it.
knowledgeLevels.2: Parts: meat (rich, dark), pelt (warm, nearly waterproof). Lives in bank dens and cattail lodges; eats everything green near the water.
knowledgeLevels.3: Hunt: set at the den mouth at dusk, or on the feeding platforms. It dives the second it spooks — chasing it is a losing argument with the creek.
knowledgeLevels.4: Mastery: muskrats mark their runs with musk — the smell IS the map. Trap the run, not the water. Pelts prime in late fall; a winter lodge means a fat muskrat.

unknown: a ripple that isn't a fish, sliding along the bank
behaviorDesc: Builds bank dens and cattail lodges, marks its runs with musk. When it dives, it stays down — longer than you can hold your nerve.
huntText: A V of ripples slides off the cattails — then nothing. The muskrat is already under the bank, listening to your feet.
tell: a sliding ripple line along the bank, and a sweet-musky smell on the water.
